The core of the course. Six lecture decks and ten exercises covering multiple
regression itself and the four assumptions that most often fail in applied work:
linearity, no omitted variables, no collinearity, and constant error variance.

## Slides

| Deck | Covers |
|:--|:--|
| 🖥 [Multiple linear regression](/slides/30-multiple-regression/multiple-regression.html) | Several predictors at once; holding other things equal in practice |
| 🖥 [Linearity](/slides/30-multiple-regression/linearity.html) | Diagnosing non-linearity; fixing it with transformations |
| 🖥 [Omitted variable bias](/slides/30-multiple-regression/ovb.html) | What leaving a variable out does to the estimates you keep |
| 🖥 [Collinearity](/slides/30-multiple-regression/collinearity.html) | When predictors carry the same information; VIF and diagnostics |
| 🖥 [Heteroscedasticity](/slides/30-multiple-regression/heteroscedasticity.html) | Non-constant error variance and robust standard errors |
| 🖥 [Hedonic prices model](/slides/30-multiple-regression/hedonic-regression.html) | A full applied example decomposing prices into characteristics |

: {tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}
